newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares down at noon on cautious mood.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares down at noon on cautious mood.

text.p: Shanghai's B share index was down at midday on Friday on profit-taking with investors cautious over the market trend after Thursday's plunge, brokers said.
The B index slid 0.885 points or 0.95 percent to 97.450 points on volume of 14.803 million shares worth $10.103 million, compared with $9.844 million on Thursday.
No solid measures to cool down the market were made public today despite investors concerns which pushed the market down sharply on Thursday, but market sentiment was cautious, brokers said.

"Speculative domestic investors have become cautious after yesterday's plunge," one broker said. "They were seen offsetting their positions to take profit in the morning, which pulled down the index."

"B shares prices are still much lower than their counterparts on the A share market, so the B shares will rise again after the current correction if no government crackdown measures emerge," another broker said.
Of 43 shares, 42 traded, with 24 down, seven flat and 11 up.
Bicycle maker Phoenix Co was the biggest loser on poor 1996 results, slipping $0.014 or 7.14 percent to $0.182 on volume of 18,000 shares.
The market giant Shanghai Chlor Alkali Chemical was the most actively traded stock on institutional selling, down $0.006 or 1.65 percent to $0.358 on volume of 2.2 million shares.
Shanghai's A share index rose on a technical rebound after yesterday's plunge, but the outlook is unclear, brokers said.
The A index gained 26.832 points or 1.83 percent to 1,494.693 points on volume of 405.6 million shares worth 6.1 billion yuan.
The SSE30 blue chip index moved up 52.037 points or 1.27 percent to 4,144.163 points.
Yunnan Baoshan Cement was the biggest gainer on talk that a large share had been acquired by an institution, surging 0.83 yuan or 10.00 percent 9.68 yuan on volume of 4.2 million shares.
